1778822222-propagation-sso-edge-cache.json

Maya: Hey folks — customer AcmePayments hit a sudden spike of 401s right after we rolled their API key rotation this morning. They say it started at ~09:12 UTC and only for requests routed to eu-west-1. Error body: `{"error":"unauthorized","message":"invalid_api_key"}`.

Raj: cc @Maya — looking at the control plane logs. I see the new key was written to Vault at 09:10 but Vault->edge sync shows a few 403s when trying to unwrap with the KMS alias `projects/secure/kms/aliases/redwood-eu`. Possible alias permission mismatch.

Liam: Can you paste the exact Vault response? also confirm whether they use our hosted SDK or a proxy in front.

Maya: Customer uses our hosted API via an edge proxy (Acme's sidecar) and we also see `403: kms: permission denied` in the unwrap traces. Sample control-plane log:

```
control-plane: vault.write(key=acct-482/new_key) => 200
kms.unwrap(alias=redwood-eu, ciphertext=...) => 403 PermissionDenied
edge-sync: failed to decrypt token -> fallback stale key used
```

Zara: That suggests the new key material couldn't be decrypted at the moment of rotation, so some proxies kept serving the old key which we revoked. Classic revocation race. What's the TTL/propagation window for the vault sidecar?

Raj: Sidecar polling is 30s for live sync, but unwrap failures cause sidecar to mark the secret as invalid and return 401s until a successful unwrap. I see a short window (09:10:12–09:13:05) where ~4k requests got 401.

Maya: Customer notes intermittent 401s across multiple hosts, then cleared after ~3 minutes. They hit our support SLA about billing because requests that failed still counted in their meter (they say they were charged).

Liam: Billing should not charge for failed auths — but we do log consumed tokens at different layers. Filing billing ticket if there's a mismatch. For now we need to: 1) validate KMS alias IAM policy, 2) confirm Vault rewrap logic succeeded after the window, 3) check edge-proxy caching behavior.

Raj: I just ran an `iam test` on the KMS principal used by vault-unwrapper: it had a missing `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt` permission in EU alias's policy due to a stale terraform change. I pushed a fix and replumbed at 09:14:30.

Maya: Great. Customer asked for repro steps so they can avoid this during their coordinated rotations. Any concise steps?

Zara: Repro recipe we validated:
- Create a new key in Vault and trigger rotation
- Temporarily remove/unset KMS decrypt permission for the Vault service account (simulate accidental policy drift)
- Send continuous requests through edge-proxy pointing at eu region
- Revoke old key in Vault (what we did via `vault kv metadata put -custom-delete=true`)
Expect: some hosts that can't unwrap will return 401 until unwrap succeeds; if old key is revoked before unwrap works, 401 spike occurs.

Maya: Add note: edge proxies may cache authorization material for up to 60s; if they cache the new (invalid) state or the revoked token, you can see extended errors. Also our CDN occasionally caches a 401 for a short TTL if origin returned it — so beware edge-caching of error responses.

Liam: Mitigation checklist we applied for AcmePayments:
1) Temporarily reactivated the old key entry in Vault (mark as active) so edge could fallback — rolled back revocation.
2) Fixed KMS IAM on alias and forced a rewrap for the new key; verified unwrap success in logs.
3) Pushed a sidecar config update to tolerate unwrap failures for 120s instead of marking secret invalid immediately (gives time for rewrap).
4) Issued a billing reconciliation to ensure failed requests during 09:10–09:14 were zero-rated.

Raj: Follow-up: we should add a pre-rotation check that validates KMS alias permissions and runs a dry-unwrap to confirm decryption works before finalizing revocation. I'll open a PR against infra-runbooks.

Maya: I'll send the customer a summary and the repro steps. They want a postmortem doc and confirmation their billing was corrected.

deploy-bot: Incident tag created: `INC-2026-03-15-rotation-eu-401s` Assigned -> Infra + Support.

Zara: Also let's schedule a cross-team runbook review — the sidecar behavior (invalidate vs. degrade) needs to be standardized so rotations don't produce billing-impacting failures.

Maya: Thanks all — keeping this thread open until the postmortem lands. :thumbsup:
